Subject: RE: Peregrine Labs — carveout for customer prompts & Order Form redline (internal)

Team — reviewed Peregrine's redline. Below are two alternative tracks we can present to the customer. Both are intended to be narrow, operationally enforceable, and align to our risk profile. I've attached a clean redline with these proposals (redline_suggested_Peregrine_v1.docx).

Option 1 (Customer Prompt Carveout + Timebox):
- Redwood shall not use customer-supplied prompts or prompt/response pairs ("Customer Data") to train, fine-tune, or update model weights for a period of 24 months from the Effective Date.
- Customer may opt-in later with written consent and a separate addendum.
- We retain telemetry rights limited to system metrics (latency, error rates) and non-identifying usage statistics for capacity planning.

Option 2 (Narrow Feedback License + Aggregate Signals):
- Redwood may collect aggregated and de-identified metrics derived from Customer Data for the sole purpose of service quality improvements (e.g., toxicity filters, latency optimizations), provided such data cannot be reverse-engineered to reconstruct original prompts/outputs.
- Any use beyond aggregate metrics (model retraining, publishing benchmarks that include customer-derived content) requires Customer's express written permission.

Recommended approach: Offer Option 1 as the baseline (customer-facing carveout) and Option 2 as a permissive path if Peregrine explicitly agrees to anonymized aggregates. Operational notes:
- Our telemetry ingestion pipeline will need a filter to mark Peregrine traffic as "no-train" so it is excluded from labeled training datasets and fine-tune jobs. Ben/Jordan, can you confirm ETA to implement tagging and enforcement?

If we go this route, I'll produce redline language that replaces Peregrine's broader prohibition with the timeboxed carveout + aggregate telemetry carve. That will be easier to get procurement to sign and gives Peregrine the protections they want.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redline_suggested_Peregrine_v1.docx (Word doc, 42KB)

Erin / Peregrine contracts team — thanks for the patience while we reviewed. Summary and next steps below.

What Redwood can accept now (summary):
- We will accept a Customer Prompt carveout that prohibits Redwood from using raw prompt+response pairs to train or update model weights for 24 months from the Effective Date.
- We will provide a limited feedback license to collect aggregated and de-identified signals solely for service quality (latency, error rates, anonymized model performance metrics). These aggregates will not be used to retrain models unless Peregrine provides express written consent.

Key operational controls we will apply:
- Peregrine traffic will be tagged in ingestion as "no-train" so it is excluded from labeled training datasets and fine-tune jobs.
- Telemetry (aggregates only) will be retained for up to 180 days for product quality and capacity planning, per our standard telemetry retention policy unless otherwise negotiated.

Attachments & artifacts:
- Attached: Peregrine_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf (PDF, 63KB) with the proposed clause in Section 4.2 and an added opt-in addendum for future consent.
- DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/agreements/PL-2027-072 (for the Order Form once countersigned)

Requested confirmation from Peregrine:
1) Please confirm acceptance of the carveout + aggregate telemetry approach.
2) If accepted, let us know whether procurement wants the 24-month timebox shortened to 12 months or extended.
3) If you want a legal-to-legal call, propose 2x 30-min windows next week and I will coordinate internal attendees.

If Peregrine confirms quickly, we can circulate a final DocuSign package by EOD Wednesday.
